title: Codex execution-quality observability gap
objective: Extend the existing Codex research execution-observability path so completed remediation can distinguish first-patch success, bounded pre-edit exploration, rework or test cycles, and attributable failure or telemetry-unavailable states when those facts are deterministically available. Preserve current queue authority, transition/completion semantics and backward compatibility. Never fabricate unavailable telemetry, create a new agent/engine/test, rank models as authority, or use telemetry to promote, merge or resolve a task automatically.
allowed_change_scope: tests/remediation/directly related Codex intake, completion-receipt and execution-ledger tests
research/codex/README.md only if the existing observability contract requires synchronized documentation

evidence.summary: Current Investering control-plane main used for the bounded gap audit.
Current completion receipt records candidate/task identity, PR, merge commit, verification evidence and post-fix gate, but no execution-quality telemetry or explicit telemetry-unavailable state.
Current execution ledger records lifecycle and task-contract transitions, but not first-patch success, pre-edit exploration, edit/test rework cycles or evidence-backed failure attribution.

Pinned upstream experiment demonstrates process metrics such as tool/read calls before first edit, first model-triggered test pass, edits after first test, total edits, final success, latency and token usage, while warning that time-to-first-edit is not a quality score by itself.

Pinned upstream trajectory-verifier example preserves dimensioned process evidence rather than collapsing execution into a single score, supporting bounded failure-attribution observability rather than autonomous self-modification.

reproduction: On current main 5cc5b0a293fc0abdcc53aa211f78de2f419c8a80, inspect scripts/remediation/write_codex_research_completion_receipt.py and scripts/remediation/merge_codex_research_intake.py. Construct two synthetic research-origin completion scenarios with the same valid candidate/task hashes, PR/merge evidence, VERIFIED completion status and final RESOLVED lifecycle state: scenario A reaches a passing patch on its first model-triggered test with no rework; scenario B fails the first test and requires multiple edit/test cycles. The current completion receipt and execution event have no structured fields that can distinguish these execution-quality paths. Confirm also that missing historical process telemetry cannot be recovered deterministically from the current receipt itself.

positive: A production-shaped completion fixture can persist a small structured execution-quality block or equivalent fields for deterministically supplied telemetry, including explicit first-patch/test outcome, bounded pre-edit exploration and rework/test-cycle information where available.
The receipt hash covers the added telemetry and merge_codex_research_intake.py carries the relevant observability fields into the execution state or ledger without changing queue authority.

A bounded evidence-backed failure-attribution field or telemetry status can distinguish captured, partially captured and unavailable execution evidence without collapsing the result into one opaque quality score.
Existing completion receipts created before this change remain valid and resolvable; absent telemetry is represented as unavailable/not captured rather than zero, pass, fail or inferred history.
Directly related remediation tests pass for both a telemetry-present completion and a legacy telemetry-absent completion.
negative: Missing process telemetry must never be inferred from PR count, merge status, elapsed calendar time, commit count or historical lifecycle state.
Execution-quality fields must not change CODEX_READY classification, candidate authority, merge permission, RESOLVED semantics, market/framework authority or post-fix gates.
Do not create a new agent, engine, active research test, scoring authority, model leaderboard or autonomous prompt/self-modification loop.
Do not backfill historical completion receipts with invented first-patch, tool-call, token, rework or failure-attribution values.
Do not require upstream ai-agent-book code or any new external dependency at runtime.
